verses.text: This is the letter that the prophet Jeremiah sent from Jerusalem to the elders who were left among the exiles, and to the priests, the prophets, and all the people Nebuchadnezzar had taken into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon.
This was after King Jeconiah, the queen mother, the court officials, the leaders of Judah and Jerusalem, the craftsmen, and the metalworkers had left Jerusalem.
He sent it with Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah, whom Zedekiah king of Judah sent to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. The letter said:
This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says to all the exiles I sent from Jerusalem to Babylon:
"Build houses and live in them. Plant gardens and eat what they grow.
Get married and have sons and daughters. Find wives for your sons and give your daughters in marriage, so that they also have sons and daughters. Grow in number there. Do not decrease.
Work for the peace and well-being of the city where I sent you into exile. Pray to the LORD for it, because if it has peace, you will have peace."
This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: "Do not let the prophets and fortune-tellers among you deceive you. Do not listen to the dreams you encourage them to have.
They are prophesying lies to you in my name. I did not send them," says the LORD.
This is what the LORD says: "When seventy years are over for Babylon, I will come to you and keep my good promise to bring you back to this place.
For I know the plans I have for you," says the LORD, "plans for peace and not for disaster, to give you hope and a future.
Then you will call on me, and you will come and pray to me, and I will listen to you.
You will look for me and find me when you search for me with all your heart.

I will let you find me," says the LORD, "and I will bring you back from captivity. I will gather you from all the nations and all the places where I have driven you," says the LORD. "I will bring you back to the place from which I sent you into exile."
You may say, "The LORD has raised up prophets for us in Babylon."
But this is what the LORD says about the king who sits on David's throne and about all the people who live in this city, your relatives who did not go with you into exile.
This is what the LORD of Armies says: "Look, I will send war, famine, and disease against them. I will make them like rotten figs, so bad they cannot be eaten.

I will chase them with war, famine, and disease. I will make them something terrible to all the kingdoms of the earth, an object of horror, shock, mockery, and disgrace among all the nations where I drive them.
This is because they have not listened to my words," says the LORD, "which I sent to them again and again through my servants the prophets. And you exiles have not listened either," says the LORD.
So listen to the LORD's message, all you exiles whom I have sent from Jerusalem to Babylon.

This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says about Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah, who are prophesying lies to you in my name: "Look, I will hand them over to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will kill them right before your eyes.
Because of them, all the exiles from Judah in Babylon will use this curse: 'May the LORD make you like Zedekiah and Ahab, whom the king of Babylon burned in the fire.'

For they have done disgraceful things in Israel. They committed adultery with their neighbors' wives and spoke lies in my name, things I did not command them. I know it, and I am a witness to it," says the LORD.
Tell Shemaiah the Nehelamite:

"This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: You sent letters in your own name to all the people in Jerusalem, to Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest, and to all the priests. You wrote,
'The LORD has made you priest in place of Jehoiada the priest, to be in charge of the LORD's temple. You should put any madman who acts like a prophet in the stocks and in chains.
So why have you not stopped Jeremiah from Anathoth, who acts like a prophet among you?
He has sent a message to us in Babylon saying, The exile will be long. Build houses and live in them. Plant gardens and eat what they grow.'"
Zephaniah the priest read this letter to Jeremiah the prophet.
Then the LORD's message came to Jeremiah:
"Send this message to all the exiles: 'This is what the LORD says about Shemaiah the Nehelamite: Shemaiah has prophesied to you, even though I did not send him, and he has made you trust in a lie.

So this is what the LORD says: I will punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his descendants. None of his family will be left among these people, and he will not see the good things I will do for my people, says the LORD, because he has preached rebellion against the LORD.'"
